# Gavé

> Gavé grows Espadín and Salmiana agave with 50 partner families across some 500 hectares of regenerated land in San Luis Potosí, Mexico. It supplies agave piña to beverage producers and to inulin and agave syrup buyers, and it is the group behind Tajacú mezcal.

How the agave is grown is the point. In the Huasteca Potosina, Espadín replaces sugarcane fields exhausted by decades of monoculture, planted with companion crops to rebuild the soil. On the Altiplano potosino, Salmiana grows at lower density inside an agro-silvo-pastoral system: it reforests, holds soil against erosion, feeds livestock and, at maturity, goes to mezcal. Local communities are partners across the whole cycle, not hired labour; the most developed case is with Tének communities of the Huasteca Potosina. Gavé also grows Sisal, Atrovirens, Cupreata, Potatorum and other species.

## Pages

- [Home](/): How Gavé's agave is grown (Huasteca and Altiplano), partner communities, agave raw material for beverages, inulin and syrup (including forward purchase of lots), Tajacú mezcal, and who to contact for what.
- [Services](/servicios): Regenerative agriculture and livestock advisory for ranch owners, agave plants by the lot, and reforestation programmes and tenders for companies, foundations and institutions.
- [Nursery — Espadín & Salmiana](/vivero): Field-ready agave plants, quoted by lot.
- [Espadín pups](/hijuelos-espadin): Espadín pups adapted to the Huasteca Potosina, quoted by lot.
- [Blog](/blog): Field notes on agave, regenerative agriculture and arid-land restoration, in Spanish and English.
- [Contact](/contacto): One form for buyers, distributors, ranch owners, programmes and partners.
- [Tajacú](https://www.tajacu.com): Tajacú mezcal, the spirits brand of the Gavé group.
